# Auth Security Checklist: Logout Requirements Quality

**Purpose**: Review the quality of the logout requirements for completeness, clarity, consistency, and coverage before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-08-15
**Feature**: [scrum-7-auth-logout.md](../stories/scrum-7-auth-logout.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Are the required logout inputs and authentication preconditions explicitly defined for the endpoint, including the expected JWT format and placement? [Completeness, Spec §AC-1, Spec §Tech-Context]
- [ ] CHK002 - Is the persistence mechanism for token revocation clearly specified as a database-backed blacklist and are both access and refresh tokens included in scope? [Completeness, Spec §AC-2, Spec §AC-5]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are the success and failure response contracts defined in measurable terms for all named scenarios, including HTTP code and payload shape? [Completeness, Spec §AC-3, Spec §AC-4, Spec §Gherkin]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are audit and logging requirements stated for failed auth or revoke attempts, including the minimum data captured without exposing secrets? [Completeness, Spec §Implementation Checklist, Constitution §1.4]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 - Is the term "invalida token en blacklist" defined with implementation-neutral but testable rules for when a token becomes unusable? [Clarity, Spec §AC-2]
- [ ] CHK006 - Is the revoke action specified with enough precision to distinguish between a valid logout request and a request with an expired or malformed token? [Clarity, Spec §AC-4, Spec §Gherkin]
- [ ] CHK007 - Are returned response messages and status codes for success and invalid-token cases written in a way that avoids ambiguity across clients and tests? [Clarity, Spec §AC-3, Spec §AC-4]
- [ ] CHK008 - Is the requirement for "token no puede ser reutilizado" expressed as a concrete postcondition that can be checked repeatedly across protected endpoints? [Clarity, Spec §AC-4, Spec §Scenario]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 - Do the success, revocation, and reuse scenarios align without contradicting each other on token lifecycle behavior? [Consistency, Spec §AC-2, Spec §AC-4, Spec §Gherkin]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are the security requirements for logout consistent with the project-wide auth principles regarding JWT usage, role scope, and audit logging? [Consistency, Constitution §1.4, Spec §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK011 - Is the requirement to revoke refresh tokens consistent with the stated auth model and with any downstream token rotation or refresh flows that may exist? [Consistency, Spec §AC-5, Constitution §1.4]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK012 - Are the acceptance criteria measurable enough to support objective review, such as exact status codes, payload expectations, and post-logout token rejection behavior? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §AC-1, Spec §AC-2, Spec §AC-3, Spec §AC-4]
- [ ] CHK013 - Can each Gherkin scenario be mapped to one or more objective acceptance criteria without hidden assumptions about implementation details? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §Gherkin]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK014 - Are primary, alternate, and exception flows covered for valid logout, invalid token, expired token, and already-revoked token reuse, or are any such flows explicitly excluded? [Coverage, Spec §Gherkin, Gap]
- [ ] CHK015 - Are recovery or retry requirements defined for transient database or token validation failures so that the system behavior remains deterministic? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Gap]
- [ ] CHK016 - Are requirements specified for zero-state or edge cases such as missing Authorization header, empty token, and token with mismatched subject or type? [Coverage, Edge Case, Gap]

## Non-Functional and Dependency Quality

- [ ] CHK017 - Are security and data-protection requirements defined for token blacklist storage, including no plaintext token disclosure and safe handling of JWT identifiers in persistence? [Non-Functional, Constitution §1.4, Gap]
- [ ] CHK018 - Are external dependencies and assumptions documented for PostgreSQL storage, JWT validation, and protected-endpoint enforcement, including expected runtime environment requirements? [Dependencies & Assumptions, Spec §Technical Context, Gap]
- [ ] CHK019 - Are requirements explicit about which tokens are invalidated when logout is called, and does the spec distinguish access-token logout from refresh-token logout when both forms exist? [Ambiguity, Spec §AC-2, Spec §AC-5]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- The current story includes the key must-haves: database blacklist revocation, successful logout response, invalid token rejection, and refresh-token revocation.
